title: Why is the new Call of Duty game getting backlash?
description:
Modern Warfare 4 - the latest Call of Duty game - was already deemed controversial before its release. The main storyline depicts a fictional conflict in the Korean Peninsula, with North Korea invading the South. That’s upset many Koreans: More than one million people died in the real Korean War, and technically North Korea and South Korea remain at war because a peace deal was never signed. Loyal fans of the video game franchise were not put off by the controversial story line, as developers Activision have been inspired by real-life events in the past. But some fans discovered real footage from the Itaewon crowd crush, a tragedy completely unrelated to conflict, in the game. Victims’ families were horrified and complained. BBC Newsbeat’s Riyah Collins and Jake Kwon, the BBC’s correspondent in Seoul, explain how the game has been received.

summaryEn: The latest Call of Duty: Modern Warfare video game has sparked strong backlash in South Korea for depicting a fictional North Korean invasion, tapping into painful Korean War memories and ongoing geopolitical tensions. Controversy deepened when players identified real news footage of the 2022 Itaewon crowd crush in the game's opening cinematic. Following anger from victims' families and players, developer Activision apologized and promised to remove the footage in an upcoming update.
